Really appreciated complementary daycare for our first visit. The staff was super helpful and helped me with short notice.

UPDATE: Continued Unprofessional Customer Service at Dallas Pet Den

Unfortunately, my experience with Dallas Pet Den has continued to go downhill.

After my experience on August 20, I called today to request a refund for the remaining daycare services since, based on everything that has happened, I will not be returning with my dogs.

I also wanted to address the comments that were placed in their system regarding me as a customer and discuss how I was treated during my previous visit. Instead of having a professional conversation or attempting to resolve the situation, Lori, the manager, hung up on me.

I have to say, I was shocked.

Mistakes happen. Customer service issues happen. What matters is how a business handles them. Where I work, we believe in doing the right thing, and if we fail a customer, we own it, apologize, and ask what we can do to make things right.

Unfortunately, that has been the complete opposite of my experience with Dallas Pet Den.

At this point, my concern goes beyond the poor customer service I experienced. When a paying customer raises legitimate concerns about communication, treatment, and how their dogs were handled, I would expect management to listen and try to resolve the issue—not hang up on the customer.

And honestly, it leaves me wondering: If this is how they treat their customers, how are they treating the dogs when their owners aren't there?

I want to reiterate that the groomer I worked with was wonderful and the grooming itself was excellent. My concerns are specifically with the daycare experience, management, communication, and customer service.

This has been an incredibly disappointing experience, and I will not be bringing my dogs back to Dallas Pet Den.

Very Disappointing Daycare Experience — Grooming Was Excellent

I was initially very cautious about taking my dogs to Dallas Pet Den because I had seen several negative reviews regarding grooming. At the time, however, I was only interested in daycare, not grooming.
Even getting started was difficult. Their online registration process was extremely confusing and not user-friendly. After finally submitting both dogs’ information and vaccination records, I waited two days and never heard from anyone. I also tried calling several times but repeatedly found myself on hold, eventually hanging up.
I ultimately went into the facility in person and spoke with a woman who told me she had been there for over 23 years. I explained my concerns about the registration process, lack of communication, difficulty reaching someone by phone, and the negative reviews I had seen. She apologized, assured me she would help, and got us set up for daycare. We went ahead and purchased daycare packages because I felt comfortable giving them a chance.
I will say that the grooming experience itself was outstanding. I met the groomer, who has more than 20 years of experience, and she was wonderful to work with. My dog's groom was excellent, and she deserves a 10/10.
Unfortunately, my experience with the front-of-house staff was the complete opposite.
When I went to pick up my dogs and pay for the grooming service, the employee assisting me was extremely short, curt, and unfriendly. When I asked where my groomed dog was, I was told, “I don't know, probably in a suite.” When I asked about my other dog after hearing him barking, I was told, “Probably.” There was no explanation, communication, or attempt to help.
I left and planned to return around 6 PM, but I felt uneasy about the entire situation and decided to come back sooner. That's when I learned that my dogs had been separated for essentially the entire day. My understanding is that once a dog is groomed, they don't return to daycare. That's perfectly fine—but no one explained that to me when I dropped them off.
Had I known that my dogs would be separated for the day, I absolutely would have come back and picked them both up after the grooming appointment. They are brothers who are accustomed to being together, and I would never knowingly choose to have them separated all day.
When I brought this concern up, rather than receiving an apology or an explanation, I was met with attitude. I was told that there were notes in their system describing me as “rude.” I found that incredibly disappointing. I explained that I didn't need an attitude; I simply wanted my concerns addressed and wanted my dogs.
What happened next made the situation even more concerning. I watched another customer's dog come out of the boarding area without a leash, running toward its owner while I was standing nearby with my dogs. Then, when my groomed dog was brought up, he was also brought out without a leash, and I was asked through a partially closed door to hand over the leashes.
The entire experience felt extremely unprofessional and lacking in basic customer service and communication.
I want to be very clear that the groomer was fantastic. Her work was excellent, and I would absolutely recommend her based on my experience with her.
However, based on my experience, I would not recommend Dallas Pet Den for daycare. The communication, customer service, handling of the dogs, and overall experience were extremely disappointing.
There was also an unpleasant smell in the lobby during my visits, which added to the overall impression of the facility.
I gave this business a chance despite the negative reviews I had initially seen, and unfortunately, my experience confirmed many of my concerns. My dogs will not be returning for daycare.
Grooming: 10/10
Daycare/customer service: 0/10
I hope management takes this feedback seriously because the grooming service itself is excellent, but the front-of-house experience and communication need significant improvement.
Aubrey is the best. She loves our dog and she is patient with our old and beautiful dog. Thank you  Aubrey. Joy and Sherry

I boarded my dogs here in the VIP room with camera access. Pros: I’ve had bad boarding experiences before, and so I appreciated the extra time that the team took answering my endless questions during intake and arranging the stay. I also have extremely limited funds as a teacher with three senior pets, and I appreciated that the staff answered my questions about pricing. Staff were immediately responsive whenever I actively reached out and pointed out that something had not been done or that I saw my dog on the camera asking to go out or sitting in a puddle of liquid or something. Staff responded even beyond business hours. My money was refunded when I sent photos of my dog’s flaking skin after the “moisturizing oatmeal bath,” no questions asked, and without me even having to ask, although I haven’t checked my statement to see if that charge was refunded. I’m going to assume she did process it. They gave me one complimentary night for being a new client. That was helpful. My male dog rarely likes male handlers, and he loved one male staff member in particular at Dallas Pet Den. I think that says a lot. They listened to the litany of my female dog’s ailments and took me seriously, and they were careful to keep her cool while also giving her some playtime, I think. There are no cameras where I could see them playing, but I did see that she was not always in her room. Also, I really appreciated that I was able to walk right in off the street and go on a tour of the facility. That said a lot about the confidence they have in the quality of their facility, and I don’t disagree. They helped me choose the right kind of room for my dogs, and I like that they have a quieter area away from the chaos that is better suited for anxious, senior animals - but you will pay a premium for it. Still, it is an option that not every facility offers. ICons: My female dog came home with significant bruising across her chest. The staff did investigate, and we can only conclude that this came from some rough play during playtime. They even had a photo they had taken of a wound, so they were prepared to address it with me if I asked, but they decided not to mention it. I would have preferred that they tell me that she was injured rather than waiting until I returned home and removed her harness to see the horrific bruises beneath. Despite paying for exit baths which was a huge expense on my limited budget, my dogs stank like pee, and I had to wash them when we got home. It was that sickly boarding facility smell. On top of that, their skin was so dry that it was flaking off. Worse yet, I was charged extra for the “moisturizing bath,” but I wasn’t told this when I selected it at check in. I thought it was just an option like you could have regular shampoo or the sensitive skin shampoo. There was no mention of an up charge. I’d like to say here that hairless dogs like mine do not have special skin; they have normal dog skin, just no fur. So any other dog getting that “moisturizing bath” is also flaky beneath all their fur; on my dogs you just see it. Some little things also when overlooked: the chew toy I sent for my dog’s anxiety wasn’t put in their room and I had to call and ask. They were not given separate beds as we had pre-arranged (they never sleep together) I had to call and ask. It was just difficult to be on vacation when I had supposedly set up all these things ahead of time only to find that much of it wasn’t being done. I can only imagine if I hadn’t gotten the room with the camera!
Overall, if you can afford it, I would recommend this facility. I felt that the people in charge were ethical and responsive to my inquiries. They treated me fairly and showed genuine care for my animals’ needs within the limitations of boarding facility management. As at any business, some staff were more invested than others. I didn’t get the sense that my animals were in danger or mistreated at any time, and many of their staff were extremely invested in establishing a relationship with my animals and effectively managing their health and happiness.

The attention to detail and professionalism she brings every appointment is the reason we continue to come back. We are so grateful to have found her — I wouldn’t trust anyone else with our dogs.
The staff is very friendly and professional

Cats seemed stressed :(  I went to check out the Pet Den. The people seemed nice, but the room for cats was so bright and loud. The place also smelled bad, which I guess isn't surprising with all of the animals? All of the dogs were jumping frantically outside the door when we walked by and the cats  were in a separate room, but could hear all of the barking (likely all day). The cages were ok but rather small. Cats generally do not like noise and like places to hide when they are stressed. I would like to see this center make this room more cat-friendly and quieter. My cat has anxiety and this place is a no for us, unfortunately. If these changes were made, we would reconsider. Thanks

We took our dog to daycare here after seeing so many reviews, and after 4 visits, we will never be back. They do not use the outdoor space advertised online, they do not have the cameras they said they have, and our dog came home COVERED in other dogs urine everyday. They never told us the outdoor area was closed, so our dog spent 4 days being traumatized by laying in other dogs pee and never going outside when they said he was. His anxiety has significantly increased, and we were so disappointed in our experience. The employees were very kind and I don’t blame them at all, just really frustrating that none of this was communicated. Why would we pay $40 a day for our dog to stay inside, lay in other dogs urine, and come home far more stressed than he was before?
I highly recommend this business.
I am very pleased with my grooming services. They take great care of my pup.

My first time going and it will not be the last. I was so nervous about leaving my doggy but it was so worth it! Aubrey is the best hands down omg! She was so thorough and made my baby look so good! Jamieka’s customer service is one to be studied! Best experience ever.

Cons: Your dogs will always smell to the point where they need a bath after one day of daycare / boarding. Overpriced grooming / bathing ($80 for a 60 pound dog to get a bath). When I come to pick them up, the bag is almost completely empty.
